topic.subject: social
topic.title: The Mauryan empire and Ashoka
topic.scope: Chandragupta Maurya, Chanakya, Pataliputra, Kalinga war, dhamma, inscriptions, Sarnath lion capital

nodes.name: Founding of the Mauryan Empire
external_prereqs: concept of a kingdom vs empire

nodes.name: Sarnath lion capital is a symbol

misconceptions.statement: Dhamma was the Buddhist religion that Ashoka forced everyone to follow.
misconceptions.why: Students conflate Ashoka's personal conversion with state policy.
misconceptions.fix: Dhamma was a set of ethical principles for social harmony, not a religious doctrine or a forced conversion.

probe.question: Did Ashoka force his subjects to become Buddhist monks?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, he made Buddhism the state religion.

misconceptions.root_belief: a word means its everyday meaning
misconceptions.source_hint: Rosalind Driver's children's ideas in science

misconceptions.statement: Kalinga was a small village that Ashoka conquered easily.
misconceptions.why: Students underestimate the scale of ancient kingdoms.
misconceptions.fix: Kalinga was a powerful coastal region, and the war was a major, bloody conflict.

probe.question: Why did Ashoka feel sad after the Kalinga war?
probe.wrong_answer: Because he lost the battle against a small village.

misconceptions.root_belief: bigger or more means more effect

misconceptions.statement: Inscriptions were written on paper by the Mauryan kings.
misconceptions.why: Students project modern writing tools onto the past.
misconceptions.fix: Inscriptions were carved onto hard surfaces like stone pillars or rock faces to ensure they lasted a long time.

probe.question: How did people read Ashoka's messages?
probe.wrong_answer: They read them on paper scrolls distributed by the king.

misconceptions.root_belief: what you cannot see does not exist

misconceptions.statement: Chanakya was the king of the Mauryan Empire.
misconceptions.why: Students struggle to distinguish between the roles of a king and his advisor.
misconceptions.fix: Chanakya was a wise teacher and advisor who helped Chandragupta become the king.

probe.question: Who was the first Mauryan emperor?

misconceptions.root_belief: one event has one single cause

misconceptions.statement: Chandragupta Maurya was Ashoka's son and became king after him.
misconceptions.why: Students mix up the order of the Mauryan rulers and assume the famous king came last in the family line.
misconceptions.fix: Chandragupta Maurya founded the empire. His son Bindusara ruled next, and Bindusara's son Ashoka ruled after him, so Chandragupta was Ashoka's grandfather.

probe.question: How was Chandragupta Maurya related to Ashoka?

misconceptions.root_belief: Mauryan rulers' family order is unclear

misconceptions.statement: The Arthashastra was a book of Buddhist teachings written by Ashoka.
misconceptions.why: Students link every famous Mauryan text to Ashoka and to Buddhism.
misconceptions.fix: The Arthashastra is a book on politics, administration and the economy. It is traditionally credited to Chanakya (Kautilya), the minister of Chandragupta. Ashoka did not write it.

probe.question: What is the Arthashastra, and who wrote it?
probe.wrong_answer: A Buddhist book written by Ashoka.

misconceptions.root_belief: Ashoka is behind every Mauryan achievement

misconceptions.statement: Pataliputra was a small trading town that never became a capital.
misconceptions.why: Students do not know that ancient cities could be large capitals, and they confuse it with smaller towns.
misconceptions.fix: Pataliputra, near modern Patna on the Ganga, was the capital of the Mauryan Empire. It was a large and important city.

probe.question: What was the importance of Pataliputra in the Mauryan Empire?
probe.wrong_answer: It was only a small trading town and not the capital.

misconceptions.root_belief: Ancient cities were small and unimportant

misconceptions.statement: Pataliputra is in the south, near the Arabian Sea coast.
misconceptions.why: Students rely on vague map memory and mix up the location with port cities.
misconceptions.fix: Pataliputra lay in the Ganga plains in the east, at the meeting of the Ganga and Son rivers. Today it is Patna in Bihar.

probe.question: Where was Pataliputra located?
probe.wrong_answer: In south India near the sea coast.

misconceptions.statement: Kalinga is the modern state of Kerala.
misconceptions.why: The two names sound alike, and students are unsure which state is on the east coast.
misconceptions.fix: Kalinga was a region in the east of India. It is roughly today's Odisha and part of the neighbouring coast. Kerala is in the far south-west.

probe.question: Which modern state is the ancient Kalinga region?

misconceptions.root_belief: Similar-sounding place names mean the same place

misconceptions.statement: Ashoka fought the Kalinga War at the very start of his reign and then ruled in peace as a Buddhist monk.
misconceptions.why: Students shorten the story and picture Ashoka giving up his throne after the war.
misconceptions.fix: Ashoka fought the Kalinga War about eight years after he became king. He felt deep sorrow after the war and gave up conquest. He remained emperor and ruled by Dhamma.

probe.question: What did Ashoka do after the Kalinga War?
probe.wrong_answer: He left the throne and became a monk.

misconceptions.root_belief: A big change means the person left their old role

misconceptions.statement: The Dhamma Mahamattas were soldiers sent to fight wars and punish rebels.
misconceptions.why: Students link officials of an empire with armies and force because of the word 'Mahamatta' and the war theme.
misconceptions.fix: The Dhamma Mahamattas were special officials appointed by Ashoka to spread the message of Dhamma. They worked for the welfare of people and for harmony.

probe.question: What was the work of the Dhamma Mahamattas?
probe.wrong_answer: They were soldiers who fought wars and punished rebels.

misconceptions.root_belief: Royal officials mainly control people by force

misconceptions.statement: Ashoka's inscriptions were all written in Sanskrit, because it was the only language of ancient India.
misconceptions.why: Students assume one classical language for the whole period and know Sanskrit best.
misconceptions.fix: Most Ashokan inscriptions were written in Prakrit, in the Brahmi script, so that ordinary people could read them. Some were in other languages and scripts in the north-west.

probe.question: In which language and script were most Ashokan inscriptions written?

misconceptions.root_belief: One language was used everywhere in ancient India

misconceptions.statement: The Sarnath lion capital was a throne where Ashoka sat to give orders.
misconceptions.why: Students see the lions as a seat or royal furniture and miss that it was the top of a pillar.
misconceptions.fix: The Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath stood on top of a pillar. It is a symbol of the Mauryan Empire and Ashoka's message. Today it is India's national emblem.

probe.question: What was the Sarnath lion capital?

misconceptions.root_belief: Famous royal objects are furniture or personal items
